Title: Botanics Storytelling Day: Story Walks
Description: Magical things happen in the autumn, when leaves fall down, mushrooms pop up, and untold stories are waiting to be foraged. Join storytellers Allison Galbraith, David Hughes and Alette Willis to explore the gardens, unearthing stories along the way, for an afternoon of fun and magic!    These 20min sessions are designed as story walks around a section of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. Please meet at the Botanic Cottage in the Demonstration Garden and dress for the weather!    Story Walk TimetableDavid Hughes: 12.15pm | 1.45pm | 3.15pmAllison Galbraith: 12.45pm | 2.15pm | 3.30pmAlette Willis: 1.15pm | 2.45pm

Title: Torsten Bell & Dharshini David: Towards a Better Economy
Teaser: Hopeful visions of the economic future are presented here by Torsten Bell, Chief Executive of the Resolution Foundation and former Director of Policy for the Labour Party, and Dharshini David, BBC’s Chief Economics Correspondent. In conversation with…
Description: Hopeful visions of the economic future are presented here by Torsten Bell, Chief Executive of the Resolution Foundation and former Director of Policy for the Labour Party, whose book Great Britain? examines how the country can be transformed for the better. He’s joined by BBC’s Chief Economics Correspondent, Dharshini David, who, in Environomics, explores the changes already happening in our world and everyday lives thanks to the green economy. Chaired by the FT's Asia News Editor, Mure Dickie.

Title: Sasha Dugdale & Rebecca Sharp: New Myths
Teaser: How do myths – both ancient and modern – shape our lives? Two new poetry collections reckon with this question. In Long Field Loop, Rebecca Sharp explores the last decade, a turbulent time for Scottish politics and identity as well as Sharp’s personal…
Description: How do myths – both ancient and modern – shape our lives? Two new poetry collections reckon with this question. In Long Field Loop, Rebecca Sharp explores the last decade, a turbulent time for Scottish politics and identity as well as Sharp’s personal life. Meanwhile, Sasha Dugdale’s sixth collection, The Strongbox, traces the lineage of Greek mythology and epic female figures in our modern times. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

Title: Sacred Arts Festival Music at Old Saint Paul’s Church
Description: Ave Maria: Centuries of Prayer and Praise. Music and poetry for Mary, the Mother of Jesus. The highly acclaimed Choir of Old Saint Paul’s, under its director Dr John Kitchen MBE, Edinburgh City Organist, performs celebrated Marian compositions interspersed with a selection of poems also inspired by Mary. Drawing on many different periods, the programme reveals the highly contrasting styles that Mary has inspired across the centuries. The poems will be read by accomplished readers drawn from the congregation of Old Saint Paul's.
Artist: Choir of Old Saint Paul’s Church
Venue description: Historic Anglican church in the Catholic tradition, one of the original homes of Scottish Episcopacy, founded in 1689. The hidden gem of the Old Town, with numerous features of architectural and artistic interest. Father Willis organ. Descriptive leaflets available. Open daily 08:30 – 17:45 to visit, or for peace and stillness.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Sax Appeal 2024
Description: Enjoy a relaxing hour away from Fringe frenzy with Scotland’s popular Hume Saxophone Quartet. Since their first Fringe appearance in 2004, the Hume have been entertaining audiences around Scotland with their enthusiastic mix of light jazz, classics, ragtime and easy-listening music. With a repertoire that covers music from Miller to Mancini and Bach to the Beatles, there’s bound to be something for everyone.
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music. Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.

Title: Jeromaia Detto: MUSH
Description: Winner: Best Comedy Weekly Award Adelaide Fringe 2024. 'Definitely a must-see this Fringe' ***** (Glam Adelaide). MUSH is the latest edition of silliness developed by award nominated comedian Jeromaia Detto! Unlock your inner child in this one-of-a-kind, kids-show-for-adults experience. MUSH uncovers the weird mushiness of one man's mind in a nonstop hour of very silly proportions! ****½ (Xpress Mag). ****½ (Perth Happenings). **** (List UK). Best Physical Theatre and Circus and Spirit of the Fringe, Sydney Fringe 2023 (Nominated). Best Comedy Sydney Fringe 2022 (Nominated).
Venue description: Running on the Fringe for over two decades, Underbelly Cowgate is home to some of the best talent and bars you can find at the Fringe. Complete with licensed bars, a café and six vivacious venues, open 'til the wee hours.

Title: John Meagher: Big Year
Description: After a sell-out run at Dublin Fringe, host of Radio 4's The Divil's Own John Meagher makes his debut at The Gilded Balloon with his debut show Big Year. 'John is a very sharp comedian... with a subtlety to his stuff I didn't have (in younger days)' (Patrick Kielty, Irish Independent).

Title: Old God
Description: Old God is a foppish, irreverent oracle. A singer of doom. A weaver of myth. A being so old they have forgotten their own name. With beautiful costuming, painted canvas backdrop and fancy golden foot lights, this white face clown seems to have walked out of the theater houses of the 1800s. Pantomime is performed alongside improvisational feats of language. No one can keep up as Old God buries the audience beneath a sea of imagery and play spinning wildly in topic but elegantly in body.
Venue description: Buzzing, unpretentious gay club over two levels with bars and dance-floor. Every day during the Fringe we host several five-star PBH Free Fringe shows, bespoke cocktails and international beers. Kitchen open every day until 22:00. Children welcome before 21:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: Jonathan Watts: The Life and Legacy of James Lovelock
Teaser: What was it like to interview one of Britian’s greatest minds? Jonathan Watts, global environment editor at the Guardian, joins chair Paul French to discuss the in-depth conversations he had with the late scientist and environmentalist James Lovelock…
Description: What was it like to interview one of Britian’s greatest minds? Jonathan Watts, global environment editor at the Guardian, joins us to discuss the in-depth conversations he had with the late scientist and environmentalist James Lovelock. Renowned for his Gaia hypothesis (the idea that life on Earth is a self-sustaining system), The Many Lives of James Lovelock is the definitive biography of a brilliant and contradictory man. Join Jonathan as he discusses Lovelock's fascinating life with chair, Paul French.

Title: Addiction: The Truth
Description: Kevin McCarron is an experienced stand-up comedian, and a Doctor of Philosophy. He has also been a drug addict and an alcoholic. In this presentation, he will mock the most cherished beliefs which have so disastrously dominated Western attitudes to drug addiction and alcoholism for the last century.
Warnings: Audience participation, Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: Located within the four-star A&O Edinburgh Hostel, Bar 50 is a bar and restaurant offering three rooms of Free Fringe shows, drinks and tasty, locally sourced pub grub in laid-back, modern and stylish surroundings, an outdoor beer garden and balcony beer terrace.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is level access via the Cowgate entrance

Title: 50/50 – George Zacharopoulos
Description: Jokes from an award-winning comedian who headlines all over the world, followed by jokes based on audience suggestions. 50% stand-up, 50% improv. 50% me, 50% you. Tour support for Jim Jefferies, Larry Dean and Chris McCausland. 'Wicked sense of humour' ***** (TheReviewsHub.com).
Venue description: Whistlebinkies is a late-night bar open until 05:00 during the Fringe. A popular viable alternative for any nocturnal drinkers wishing to avoid the clubs. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe comedy shows in our back room from 12:00. Over-18s only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There is a single step up and then 2 steps down into the bar form the Niddry street entrance. Access customer are advised to enter via Niddry street as George the 4th entrance has 15 steps down into the bar.

Title: Stories and Drawing with Axel Scheffler
Teaser: Get ready for drawing and storytelling with Axel Scheffler. Meet the characters in brand-new book Jonty Gentoo: The Adventures of a Penguin, old favourites such as Zog and The Gruffalo, and celebrate all the different ways to be kind in picture book Kind…
Description: Get ready for drawing and storytelling with Axel Scheffler. Meet the characters in brand-new book Jonty Gentoo: The Adventures of a Penguin, old favourites such as Zog and The Gruffalo, and celebrate all the different ways to be kind in picture book, Kind. The event will be followed by a book signing.

Title: Lynn Faces
Description: Nearing 40, painfully shy, and emerging from a toxic break-up, Leah forms a punk bank inspired by Lynn from Alan Partridge. As she takes to the stage with no musical ability, will this gig push Leah further over the edge, or help her regain her confidence and find the hope she needs to move on? A funny, farcical and poignant new play, exploring the impact of abusive behaviour, the power of friendship and how silliness can be healing. Lynn Faces is a new play by multi award-winning writer Laura Horton, following her Fringe First-winning show, Breathless.
Warnings:
Audience participation, Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Strong language/swearing, More information
Contains references to abuse and coercive control and haze
Artist: Co-commissioned by New Diorama Theatre, Norwich Theatre, Theatre Royal Plymouth
Venue description: Set in the iconic former Veterinary College, Summerhall's programme is packed full of exciting and challenging theatre, dance, visual art and music from across the world and Scotland for people of all ages. Delicious food and drink is served in The Royal Dick bar plus al fresco bars and street food in our vibrant and buzzing courtyard. There is a café open all day too. Full programme available at summerhall.co.uk.
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the reception, box office, shop and café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility
. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are 9 steps up to the main entrance of Summerhall, these steps do not have a handrail. Wheelchair and limited-mobility access is via the side entrance on Summerhall Square which is clearly marked by the large vehicle gates. As you enter The Royal Dick is situated to the right (with a ramp at the rear) or there is a ramp directly ahead that leads into the main building

Title: Bellringers
Description: ‘What do you want me to say? That the world’s ending? Would that be helpful?’ The mushrooms are encroaching, fish are falling from the sky, and in a bell tower Clement and Aspinall are waiting for lightning to strike. Superstition says that the ringing of church bells can dispel a storm. When it feels like the apocalypse is here, anything is worth a shot. The Stage Producer of the Year Ellie Keel Productions, and award-winning Atticist, return to ROUNDABOUT with a debut play about being young at the end of the world. Finalist: The Women’s Prize for Playwriting 2024.
Artist: Atticist, Ellie Keel Productions and Hampstead Theatre
Venue description: Roundabout is our tourable, in-the-round, 167-seater auditorium that flat packs into a lorry and pops up all over the country. You might find it in on a football pitch in Coventry, on the Margate seafront, or by a lake in Poole. Roundabout also regularly sits in the Summerhall Courtyard during the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, hosting a jam-packed programme.
Venue accessibility:
Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The main entrance to Summerhall has 9 stone steps with no railing. Step-free access is via the side entrance on Summerhall Square. 
As you enter through the side entrance, The Royal Dick bar is situated to your right (with a ramp at the rear of the bar). There is a ramp directly ahead of you, across the courtyard, that leads to the main building

Title: Window Seat
Description: 'I became the Jeremy Clarkson of tits.' In this tender off-beat comedy, a mother and daughter survey the changes in their lives while waiting onboard a plane. One is getting used to an empty nest, the other to adulthood. They both hold high hopes for the coming trip together but, with their flight delayed, reunion proves more turbulent than anticipated. Like passengers eavesdropping, we overhear a relationship in need of renewal between two women unsure of how to navigate change. Negotiating emotional crosswinds, they surprise each other with a mischievous, zigzagging honesty.
Venue description: Paradise Green is at the heart and soul of the largest arts festival in the world, presenting a wide range of top-quality performances. Visit our beautiful and friendly venue, relax with a drink from our snack bar before your performance and soak up the true atmosphere of the Fringe.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Vault is located at the end of Merchant Street, which has a pavement running half its length and cobbled street for the final 20 metres

Title: This Stand-Up Show is Free and Happening Right Now!
Description: Sam Adamson ('Thought-provoking', Mark Watson) and Jon Hipkiss ('Great work', Jack Whitehall) join forces to present you their greatest hits in this late night split-bill stand-up show. They present their absolute gold. Their best of. This show will deliver it with both barrels. This is all killer, no filler. You get the picture. Sam is the West End New Act Finalist 2024. Jon is the Leicester Comedy Festival People's Choice Award Nominee 2024.
Venue description: 1428, Cowgate gets its name from medieval times when cattle were herded down the street on market day. Now, fast forward to today; The Carnivore compliments the heritage of Edinburgh’s meat market and this is where our ethos of great quality meat for unbeatable value was born. The fuss-free food features authentic meat-lover’s classics with a twist, paired with American-inspired whiskey cocktail. Free Fringe comedy every day during August Fringe.

Title: Baby Wants Candy
Description: Fringe fave Baby Wants Candy is back! Total Edinburgh Fringe sell-out six years running. One of the world's most popular comedy ensembles. You shout out the title, BWC makes up the musical. Some favourite recent titles: Sweeney Toddler, Tinder in the Animal Kingdom and who could forget the instant classic HotUncles.com... the Musical? Buy early – shows sell out! 'An entertainment phenomenon. I have one word for them: Go!' ***** (Scotsman). ***** (Time Out). ***** (ThreeWeeks.com). 'Critic's Choice. Truly amazing!' (New York Times).
Artist: Baby Wants Candy, The Fully Improvised Full-Band Musical
Venue description: Located directly opposite the Assembly George Square Gardens entrance, the five Studio spaces, as well as Underground, our venue come nightclub, have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe, with comfortable modern seating. The indoor Studios Bar is the perfect place to spend time between shows, with food, drinks and pool tables.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Mary, Queen of Rock!
Description: You think you know the story of Mary, Queen of Scots? Think again... The year is 1561. The Scottish Reformation has enforced an outright ban on rock'n'roll. Cue the arrival of Mary Stuart, one of the world's biggest and most iconic musical artists... who happens to be the undisputed Queen of Rock! With the Scottish nobles and her cousin in England against her – can Mary get the country rocking? Or will heads roll?
Venue description: This classic building in the heart of the New Town is now the centre of a fantastic festival hub, hosting some of the finest theatre, comedy and music from around the world. The Assembly Rooms hosts three spaces indoors: the Music Hall, Ballroom and Drawing Room, with a Spiegeltent (The Bijou) and a studio space (Front Room) outside on George Street.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Accessible entrance is through the front doors.

Title: Sylas Szabolcs: Sylas But Deadly
Description: Sylas Szabolcs is celebrating two milestones. He’s been in the UK for 10 years and is turning thirty. One is enough for a therapy session but the two combined can mean only one thing: a full hour at the Fringe. This will be his second hour of stand-up comedy. Combining his taste for the silly and the serious, topics will include dating shockers, leaving his 20s behind, the oddities of British culture, our strange relationship with mental health. All done in his signature energetic, cheeky style. 'Confident and well performed.' (TheStand.co.uk).
Venue description: In Brazil, Boteco is the friendly neighbourhood bar with lively music and atmosphere, and that’s exactly where our inspiration comes from, the traditional botecos of Rio de Janeiro. You can enjoy a refreshing Caipirinha – our signature drink and an essential part of any Brazilian celebration – or sample the infamous 'urban' menu of the streets from our delicious tapas menu.
Venue accessibility: There a stairs to access our venue downstairs. But, we would be happy to carry any wheelchair down those stairs so everyone can attend the shows. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Flichterin' Duo
Description: This harp and viola duo – unusual within Scottish traditional music – has toured Scotland as part of their larger ensemble and is now bringing their more intimate sound to the Fringe. Arianna Ranieri’s classical viola training and Sam MacAdam’s traditional harp training combine, combining elements of both in Sam and Arianna’s new compositions and arrangements. Sam pushes the boundaries of what to expect from the harp and her compositions and performances have been featured on BBC Radio 3, BBC Scotland and more. Ariana’s viola brings a darker sound to Scottish folk music.
Artist: Flichterin' Duo – Sam MacAdam and Arianna Ranieri
Venue description: The venue is on the ground floor of a classic 200-year-old Georgian townhouse looking north across the Forth from Calton Hill.
Venue accessibility: Royal Terrace is flat and approached up a gradient either from the top of Leith Walk/London Road or Abbeyhill. The basement entrance is accessed by stone steps down from street level. The main entrance to the building has access from a single stone step preceeded by a 'run-in' and three stone steps up from the pavement (see pic). There is a portable ramp to help wheelchair users enter. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The basement bar is inaccessible to wheelchairs. Four steps from pavement to main entrance door

Title: Ascension
Description: I think, for now, let's stick to my life, if you don't mind. We'll come back to my death later, at the end. In 1725, Leendert Hasenbosch is marooned on Ascension Island for the crime of sodomy. Struggling to survive, he documents his descent into isolation and madness through haunting diary entries. Dan Hazelwood adapts Lee's diary, and through his life and death explores the enduring struggle for acceptance, love, and survival. Ascension tells a heart-rending story of queer identity from centuries ago that can be felt just as keenly today.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes
Venue description: Bedlam Fringe returns with another exciting programme of theatre, dance and comedy. Uniquely located in a converted neo-gothic church at the heart of the Fringe, Bedlam Theatre is the year-round home of the Edinburgh University Theatre Company. Come watch one of our shows, or sit down for a drink or snack in our cosy Fat Cat Café.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Our venue is wheelchair accessible by way of a permanent ramp at the side entrance of the Theatre. This entrance leads directly into the auditorium so is usable only between performances. Our performance times, and those times the accessible entrance will be opened, will be detailed both on our website and on a sign outside of the entrance to the auditorium. Assistance from staff will be available

Title: The Sorries at the Bar
Description: Returning to the Jazz Bar by popular demand, the duo sing, play and banter their way through a different selection of Scottish traditional music.  Along with fine musicianship, the pair delight in offering some of the stories and history behind the famous old tunes, bringing elements of their podcast The Scottish Song Guide to the stage. 'Deliciously infectious... riotous fun' ***** (ThreeWeeks, 2012). 'Authentic, lively and hugely, hugely enjoyable' ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'A must for lovers of Scots songs' **** (EdinburghSpotlight.com). ‘Foot stomping, hand clapping, sing-along-a-Scotland – very enjoyable’ ***** (ThreeWeeks, 2023).
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, multiple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00 – 05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Access to the basement venue is by two flights of stairs down from street level

Title: Mat Wills: My Wife Took My Dad to a Brothel (I Drove)
Description: A very funny sex-positive comedy show for people with genitals and a good sense of humour. Mat Wills’ most personal show to date explores family, relationships and losing one’s sense of shame for love. Taboos broken, lessons learned. Fun by, but not for, the entire family!
Venue description: Your go-to venue for craft beer in the city centre. serving great pub grub – with performances of Free Fringe comedy shows every day from 12:00 – 21:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There are two steps up into the venue from the street. Once inside there is steps up/down into the toilet

Title: A Jaffa Cake Musical
Description: Time to decide once and for all... cake or biscuit? Inspired by the 1991 tribunal which determined the true identity of a Jaffa Cake, multi-award winning Gigglemug Theatre (Scouts! The Musical, RuneSical, Timpson: The Musical) present a brand-new family-friendly musical comedy that takes the biscuit (or cake...?). Praise for previous productions: 'Incredible!' (Bear Grylls); 'Laugh-a-minute silliness' (Daily Express); 'Winning songs' (Guardian); 'Blistering wit' ***** (TheatreWeekly.com); 'Simply brilliant' ***** (NorthWestEnd.co.uk); 'An utter masterpiece' ***** (BoxOfficeRadio.co.uk); 'A comedic triumph' ***** (WestEndEvenings.co.uk); 'Absolute bangers' **** (Stage); 'Genius' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: The Pleasance’s famous cobblestone Courtyard has been entertaining festival audiences since 1985 and is considered by many to be the very heart of the Fringe. Come join us for the best comedy, theatre and children's shows at 'the centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Customers with access requirements are encouraged to contact the venue in advance and to make themselves known to a member of the team upon arrival. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Pleasance Courtyard is located uphill when accessing the venue from Cowgate. The outdoor spaces of the venue are a mix of cobblestones and tarmacked surfaces

Title: The Cryptid Factor With Rhys Darby, Dan Schreiber and Buttons
Description: Join Rhys Darby (Flight of the Conchords, Our Flag Means Death), Dan Schreiber (We Can Be Weirdos, No Such Thing As A Fish) and Leon 'Buttons' Kirkbeck (Cameo – £39 a video, 24-hour delivery guaranteed) as they take to the stage to record live episodes of New Zealand’s longest-running podcast (allegedly). Featuring jokes, monster chat, weird tales, guest cameos and a whole catalogue of Darby sound effects – The Cryptid Factor Live promises to be an unforgettable experience, and that’s a fact – you heard it here third!
Artist: Dan Schreiber, Rhys Darby and Buttons
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, Bristo Square is where you can find a variety of venues, including the magnificent McEwan Hall, presenting theatre, musicals, comedy, cabaret and family shows early 'til late.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. This is an outdoor area with level access from both Teviot Place and Reid Hall

Title: In Recital – Sungho Kim, Tenor, with Llyr Williams, Piano (Conceived and Produced by Ian McFarlane)
Description: Sungho Kim, the South Korean tenor, in a world-premiere recital with Llyr Williams on piano. The winner of the 2023 BBC Cardiff Singer of the World Song Prize, stars with Llyr Williams, his Cardiff accompanist, in McFarlane's 2024 Edinburgh world premiere. Sungho Kim tenor's 2024 world premiere recital with Llyr Williams, also celebrates the Independence Day of Ukraine on the 24th August. Supported by The Consulate of Ukraine in Edinburgh.
Artist: Sungho Kim, tenor, with Llyr Williams, piano
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music. Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The performance area and green room are not wheelchair accessible.  A ramp leads from the street up to the front portico for general access to the building. Lift access to cafe and toilets

Title: Hot Ghoul Summer
Description: The hottest stand-up duo of the season! Anitha Sri (Bath New Act of the Year Finalist, Leicester Square Quarter-Finalist, Funny Women Quarter-Finalist) and Katie Kamola (Bath New Act of the Year Semi-Finalist 2023 and 2024, Jaguar Comedy, Poster Comedy – 'The Best Comedy Clubs in London' (Londonist.com)) present an hour of wickedly dark humour.
Artist: Anitha Sri, Katie Kamola / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: In the heart of the Royal Mile, the Canons’ Gait Bar, restaurant, ground floor and basement Cellar Bar – the original Free Fringe Venue for PBH’s Free Fringe Comedy. Children welcome before 21:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Level access to bar 15 steps to performance area

Title: And Mrs
Teaser: A funny, touching exploration of fidelity, strength, and the lengths we go to honour our commitments. When Gemma’s (BAFTA winner Aisling Bea) American fiancé (Emmy nominee Colin Hanks) dies shortly before their wedding day, she decides to marry him anyway, facing public opinion, legal challenges, and family objections. With funny and moving performances, Daniel Reisinger’s […]
Description:
A funny, touching exploration of fidelity, strength, and the lengths we go to honour our commitments. 



When Gemma’s (BAFTA winner Aisling Bea) American fiancé (Emmy nominee Colin Hanks) dies shortly before their wedding day, she decides to marry him anyway, facing public opinion, legal challenges, and family objections. 



With funny and moving performances, Daniel Reisinger’s romantic comedy is an unconventional celebration of love ‘till death do us part’. 



– Massimo Iannetti








Book now
Warnings: Death and dying, Mental illness, PTSD
Venue description:
Cameo Cinema, 38 Home Street, EH3 9LZ



Fringe Venue 450



What 3 Words location: finger images smashes.



You can book tickets for Cameo Cinema screenings in-person at our EIFF Box Office from 15-21 August.



Screenings will take place in Cameo 1 and Cameo 2.

Find out about eating and drinking at the Cameo Cinema

Title: Sarah Roberts: Silkworm
Description: An adorable debut from the world’s youngest, smallest, most normal comedian. Sarah Roberts has been condemned to live a thousand lives. She was Henry VIII in her previous life, ate her twin in the womb (not an accident), and most recently got facial reconstructive surgery. Now she’s being reborn as the person she hates most: herself. Directed by Daniel Emery and Molly Stacey. ‘Phenomenal new talent, destined for stardom’ (Catherine Bohart). ‘Remarkable’ (ThreeWeeks). ‘Certified hottie’ **** (TheSpyintheStalls.com). ‘Utterly self-absorbed’ (Chortle.co.uk). BBC Comedy Award nominee, Leicester Square New Comedian of the Year runner-up, level 9461 on Candy Crush.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: Assembly Gordon Aikman Theatre, The Box and The Crate are perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post-show refreshments. The Theatre is a purpose-built venue seating up to 500 and The Box and The Crate are intimate 74-seat studios, all hosting an array of world-class shows. The Cubicle, a purpose-built immersive venue, is located behind the Gordon Aikman Theatre.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Cobbled streets surrounding George Square Gardens

Title: Bot Brothers: A Story of Our Times
Description: Two robo-clones, born of a mad professor and separated by family and class, must find a way to love where all odds are against them. This two-man comedy from Harris Morris and Joe Smith will take you on a journey through the lives of two adolescent robo-boys navigating life in the normal human world of 1980s Liverpool. Loosely based on Willy Russell’s award-winning musical Blood Brothers (Best Musical, All Major Awards! 15 million tickets sold!) From the company behind The Lost Play of Barry Wayworm: 'Fringe at it's best'  ***** (Derek Awards).
Warnings: Audience participation, Nudity, Scenes of a sexual nature, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing
Artist: Stolen Table Collective / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: This popular bar hosts great PBH Free Fringe comedy in the arch cave every day during the Fringe. Between shows, you can watch live big screen sports or simply enjoy the bar banter with beers. Over-18s only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. Single step up to the main door, 4 steps up into the bar. There are 3 steps to the toilets

Title: Benji Waterhouse: Maddening (Work in Progress)
Description: NHS psychiatrist, comedian and Sunday Times best-selling author of You Don't Have to Be Mad to Work Here road-tests more 'humane, hilarious and eye-opening' (Guardian) tales from the psych ward for his second book. 'The Adam Kay of mental healthcare' (The Times). ***** (Telegraph).
Warnings:
Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, More information
Contains themes of mental health.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House
Venue description: During the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, The Mash House emerges as a pulsating hub of creativity and cultural exchange. Nestled in the vibrant Cowgate area of the city, this converted nightclub and event space undergoes a metamorphosis, becoming a dynamic epicentre of theatrical performances, comedy shows, live music gigs, and experimental art installations.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Hidden just off Cowgate on the stairway joining Cowgate and Guthrie Street

Title: What Matters in the End?
Description: Are you ready to ask yourself the hard questions we face within society, family, love and culture? If so, come and witness the journey of four troubled souls who unwittingly explore the depths of understanding and acceptance. Is judgement an opinion or a verdict? Do we really live? What is right and what is wrong? What are we really afraid of? Do our differences divide or unite us? What really matters in the end? Find your answers at Ivy Studios, Greenside @ George Street.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing
Venue address: The Royal Society of Edinburgh, 22-26 George Street
Venue description: With six spaces, Greenside @ George Street will become one of the largest multi-space hubs at the Fringe. We’re confident that one of our spaces will be just right for you. Add to that a beautiful indoor bar, lobby seating and that infamous Greenside charm. we couldn’t be more excited to share with our new Fringe home.

Title: Gut Feelings
Description: Sophia Jane Wilkof puts the 'irritable' in 'bowel syndrome, and she's here all the way from New York City to spill her guts to you. From courage to colitis, this vivacious Jewess will explore having the guts to follow her dreams, trusting her gut (sometimes to questionable results), battling gut health issues, and a lifetime of trying to shrink her gut. If you're ailing emotionally, mentally, or physically (and who isn't?), this gut-busting show is for you! 'A modern Mrs Maisel!' (Sophia's Mom).
Artist: Sophia Jane Wilkof / PBH's Free Fringe
Venue description: PBH Free Fringe venue on Leith Walk
Venue accessibility: No wheelchair accessible toilet

Title: A Montage of Monet
Description: Monet’s paintings are world famous. We all know his water lilies, but how much do we know of the man? This new play explores his life and loves: his two marriages, the devastating death of his first wife, followed by the erratic behaviour of his lover and the desperation prompting his suicide attempt. We become privy to his thoughts on fellow impressionists and how he coped with his failing eyesight, which tormented him. It could have stopped him painting... or did it? This one-man montage of his life will be performed by award-winning actor Stephen Smith.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes
Venue address: The Royal Society of Edinburgh, 22-26 George Street

Title: Keep the Heid and Read: A Career-Long Professional Learning Event with James Robertson
Teaser: The Scots language has been growing in popularity in schools and it’s easy to see why: it’s a playful approach to language that encourages a love of words, reading, and writing. Get inspired with James Robertson – poet, novelist and translator – as he…
Description: The Scots language has been growing in popularity in schools and it’s easy to see why: it’s a playful approach to language that encourages a love of words, reading, and writing. Get inspired with James Robertson – poet, novelist and translator – as he offers top tips for incorporating Scots into the classroom. There will be the chance to hear from other learning professionals, and Robertson will share the ethos behind Itchy Coo Publishing: an imprint he co-founded which translates bestselling children’s books into Scots. Titles include The Gruffalo’s Wean, A Series of Scunnersome Events, and Roald Dahl’s Reekin Rhymes.

Title: MILF and the Mistress
Description: Ali is living the rainbow family dream – but something is missing. It's a need her wife doesn’t understand, a sexual fantasy suppressed her whole life. Now, suburban swinging, latex and literary eroticism collide, sending her on a hilarious quest to fulfil her darkest desires. A powerhouse solo performance by Australian theatre luminary Jennifer Vuletic, in a darkly hilarious play by Jane Montgomery Griffiths. A story for anyone who wonders if not now, when? 'Writing is clever, cutting and poignant' ***** (TheatreMatters.com.au). 'Brilliant and thought-provoking' ***** (DarkStoriesTheatre.com.au). 'Vuletic is magnetic' **** (Age, Melbourne).

Description:
A middle-aged man builds a mobile religious shrine to make money in this darkly funny and moving exploration of consequences.



Confronted by the success of this get-rich-quick scheme, a crisis of conscience forces our hero into a spiral of remorse and self-examination. 



Deceptively simple and superbly acted, this elegantly subversive film doubles as an intriguing window into the diasporic Iranian community in Montreal. 



– Paul Ridd

Title: Wallace
Description: As William Wallace lies in a London dungeon awaiting trial, he knows his fate is sealed. Here we see the man behind the legend. Brought back from 2023, this is a must-see performance of power and heart. Bobby Bulloch is outstanding as he brings the life of Wallace to life, and lets the audience see the man rather than the legend. Getting rave reviews from audience members, its a must-see piece of heart-wrenching theatre. 'Just stunning' (Audience review). 'Cried for ages after watching this show' (Audience review).

Title: Hanan Issa: Halal Habibis
Description: A perfectly executed clusterf*ck masterpiece of a life story, Halal Habibis follows comedian Hanan Issa's wild journey to get married as a young Muslim woman born and raised in NYC. Having lost her mother at nine years old, Hanan dives into her childhood and reflects on how the passing of her mother affected her attitude whilst growing up towards love, relationships and Islam. Halal Habibis is genuinely a vulnerable and hilarious show that highlights the true meaning of resiliency, hope and delusions in the manifestations of a Lebanese woman.

Title: What The Veck? Songs in the Key of Strife!
Description: What happens when a songwriter invites innocent bystanders on the streets of Edinburgh to share their most embarrassing memories and comedic confessions? They end up in his show that same night! Hugely relatable, Tom Veck brings charm and warmth to this five-star show, where domestic ditties mingle with stories from his peculiar past and the confessions of strangers. His expertly crafted songs will have you on the edge of your seat wondering What the Veck is coming next! And who knows, you just might win a prize in the Naffle!

Starting back in the raucous days of the music hall, this high energy revue features much-loved and well-known songs from genre defining composers like Gershwin and Lloyd Webber – all the way through to big, modern day musical titans like Lin Manuel Miranda. Join us for a glorious celebration of the very best of West End magic!

Today, Jay Bernard, Mary Jean Chan, Will Harris, and Nisha Ramayya share their insights from that conversation in a fascinating event about collaboration, artistic practice, and found families.

Title: Think Tank: Suzy Glass & Georgina Voss
Teaser: Systems and networks govern our lives in all-encompassing – and increasingly confounding – ways. Georgina Voss, author of Systems Ultra, and strategist Suzy Glass are the ultimate tour guides in this complex age, here to show us that we don’t have to…
Description: Systems and networks govern our lives in all-encompassing – and increasingly confounding – ways. Georgina Voss, author of Systems Ultra, and strategist Suzy Glass are the ultimate tour guides in this complex age, here to show us that we don’t have to passively accept the idea that some things are too complicated to understand. Get involved in this Think Tank series encouraging deep discussion between audience members (over a drink).

Title: Flo & Joan: The Joan & Flo Show
Description: Well, it looks like it's time to get your ears syringed because acclaimed musical comedy duo Flo & Joan are taking to the stage, and they have some quote unquote music and/or comedy to fill a percentage of your time. There'll be old songs, new songs, nothing borrowed and their vocal coach is Duncan from Blue. As seen on their Amazon special Alive on Stage, Comic Relief, Live at the Apollo, the Royal Variety Performance and Russell Howard Hour. 'Goes down a storm' **** (Times). Title: The Land That Never Was
Description: The Land That Never Was tells the true story of Gregor MacGregor (yes that is his real name), a Scottish soldier-turned-conman who sold a country that literally did not exist. Blending confessional stand-up, storytelling, and a whole lot of bullshit. This is a show that looks to the past to examine where we come from, where we are now, and what the future may look like. It's a show about a group of strangers who collectively believed in something that doesn't exist... yet.

Venue description: Once a World War One military hospital and now home to Edinburgh Napier University's Business School. Craiglockhart Campus also hosts the War Poets Collection. This comprises of more than 800 items, including many unique items that Edinburgh Napier University is proud to own, such as signed first edition books, volumes of poetry by Sassoon and Owen and three original issues of The Hydra, the hospital’s magazine.

Fearlessly defying public opinion, Frank commands his comedy Luftwaffe, engaging in a spirited battle against the forces of political correctness. Through dark humour and extreme renditions, he orchestrates a unique performance that challenges norms and tickles the funny bone. In this audacious spectacle, Frank transforms historical figures into sources of amusement, inviting audiences to embrace laughter as a potent antidote. Brace yourself for an entertaining swinging escapade where wit and satire collide, creating an unapologetically humorous odyssey into the absurd.

Title: Dom Hutchins – The Big Issues
Description: Dom Hutchins – The Big Issues. Embark on Dom Hutchins' Edinburgh Fringe journey with cerebral palsy; humour and heart intertwine as he discusses his struggle with cerebral palsy. This celebration of the human spirit leaves audiences inspired, reminded that with humour and resilience, obstacles can be conquered. Don't miss this empowering show that proves laughter is transformative, leaving you ready to face challenges head-on. Join Dom for an uplifting experience that will stay with you long after the laughter fades, a testament to the power of perseverance and the triumph of the human spirit.
Venue description: We welcome you to The Raging Bull, an Edinburgh cocktail bar famous for its coffee cocktails. Our cosy bar is inspired by the eccentric yet good-natured fellow, who has become accustomed to drinking his cocktails in comfortable and stylish surroundings. Accompanied by a live, performed reading from award-winning actor and comedian, Julian Clary, this spectacular storytelling event is perfect for new and old fans of Wilde’s timeless tale of kindness and community.

Title: Sinatra: Raw
Description: 1971. Palm Springs. Frank Sinatra’s last intimate concert. His blue eyes are red rimmed with memories and regret. This is the 2am Sinatra you dream of meeting. Dangerous. Opinionated. Unpredictable. Brilliant. Part play, part concert, this brilliant piece of gig theatre has enjoyed global sell-out runs in London, New York and Los Angeles. With stunning versions of Sinatra’s songs, Richard Shelton’s critically acclaimed, multi award-winning play reveals the man behind the myth. ‘Mesmerising… A must see’ **** (Times). ‘A glorious, compelling masterpiece’ ***** (LondonTheatre1.com). ‘The audience were mesmerised and enthralled’ (WestEndWilma.com). ‘Quite simply phenomenal’ **** (BBC Music).

Cyclists can’t get to Hackton library, literacy rates are dropping, cyclists can barely name a single book, library membership is dwindling and Hackton council have to do something about it! Old grudges resurface as two departments work together to save the library. Time is running out as they have to convince you, the citizens of Hackton, to vote for the right solution. A thrill ride of a debut character hour from Derek Mitchell (Ted Lasso), whose online sketches have amassed over 250 million views and a dedicated following. ‘The biggest laughs of the night’ (TheArtsDesk.com). 'Hugely entertaining... out-and-out hilarious' (Stage). ‘One of the most astounding pieces of acting I’ve seen’ (TheOxfordCultureReview.com).

Playing a vast range of A-side blues from popular artists such as Peter Green, Freddie King, JJ Cale and more... plus the best B-side blues, as well as original songs. Their special concert programme also includes Swedish and Scottish a cappella quartets. Together, they perform in the glorious surroundings and acoustic glory of St Cuthbert’s Church. Description: A celebrated London professor falls from grace in Andrew O’Hagan’s new novel, Caledonian Road. Title: Peni Candra Rini
Teaser: Vocalist Peni Candra Rini sings to traditional percussion from her native Indonesia.
Description:
Vocalist Peni Candra Rini sings to traditional percussion from her native Indonesia.Peni Candra Rini is a sindhen: an Indonesian solo female vocalist who sings to traditional Indonesian percussion, otherwise known as gamelan. Born into a family of traditional artists and musicians from East Java, she describes herself as a ‘singer and an orator of the poetry of life’.
Her compositions and performances have won acclaim worldwide and have been described as ‘mesmerising’ (Planet Hugill) and ‘beautiful’ (The Guardian). A laureate of the 2022 Aga Khan Music Awards, Peni is also in demand worldwide as a lecturer on Indonesian music.
Her appearances have ranged from intimate performances in small Javanese villages to recent concerts with the Kronos Quartet at Carnegie Hall and the Philharmonie de Paris. Her International Festival recital will feature traditional and experimental music from her native Java.
This concert is presented and curated in partnership with the Aga Khan Music Programme. Supported by Sir Ewan and Lady Brown together with Flure Grossart.

Description:
This new exhibition explores Scotland’s critical position on the frontline of the Cold War. Over 190 objects, many on display for the first time, are brought together to tell the stories of the Scots at the centre of this global conflict. 
The exhibition draws on Scotland’s rich history of Cold War-era protest and activism, and reveals the physical remains of the conflict; the ruined bases, forgotten bunkers and decommissioned nuclear power stations still evident across the Scottish landscape.
Venue description:
Our world-class collections will take you on a journey through the history of Scotland, the wonders of nature and diverse cultures from around the globe.
Discover scientific breakthroughs and marvel at exquisite art, design and fashion from across the centuries. From the tiniest creatures to towering spacecraft and ancient times to the present day, there are thousands of stories to discover.

Description: Slow death awaits shipwreck survivors on a drifting raft. Staged at the Fringe 2023, Al Carretta's adaptation of O'Neill's heavily studied but rarely produced classic one-act is now an independent feature film for 2024 and his 23rd since 2010. An intense, brooding character study the setting is transformed. The gentleman survives his ordeal at sea, but how and at what cost? Recuperating in a sanatorium in England, is his fantastical tale of circling sharks, rotting corpses and singing sailors a real tale of survival at all costs, or is the light of a dawning madness shining?

Holmes has deduced it wasn’t Moriarty, but Doyle, jealous of his popularity, behind the near-fatal attack on him at the Reichenbach Falls. Holmes, a notable rationalist, is further irked by being constantly linked with Doyle, the famous spiritualist. When two girls claim to have photographed fairies and Doyle believes them, this disgusts Holmes. He seeks to refute the pictures, but unlocks a deeper mystery surrounding the events at Cottingley. Can logic overturn belief?

Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step-free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the reception, box office, shop and café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the first floor spaces and the basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the box office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Title: Ian Bostridge & Steven Osborne
Teaser: British singer Ian Bostridge joins Edinburgh-born pianist Steven Osborne for Franz Schubert’s visionary song cycle Schwanengesang.
Description:
British singer Ian Bostridge joins Edinburgh-born pianist Steven Osborne for Franz Schubert’s visionary song cycle Schwanengesang.British singer Ian Bostridge has long been celebrated as one of the world’s most perceptive interpreters of Franz Schubert’s compositions. Bostridge brings alive the composer’s achingly beautiful melodies. Edinburgh-born pianist Steven Osborne joins Bostridge on stage for one of the composer’s most visionary vocal works. 
Schubert never conceived his visionary Schwanengesang as a song cycle. In fact, was put together shortly after his death by his publisher. Nonetheless, its 14 songs balance profound melancholy with a consoling sense of hope. Themes of lost love, regret and fear are explored as Bostridge and Osborne separate the song cycle’s settings of poetry by Ludwig Rellstab and Heinrich Heine. In between they perform a collection of Schubert’s earlier songs, from the operatic Sehnsucht to the folk-like Der Wanderer an den Mond. Description:
A richly poetic and moving film about a young person journeying to bury their lover in the heart of the Peruvian jungle. 



Slow revelations and reflections begin to paint a picture of the deceased and a life before as we learn of a troubling past haunted by intimidation and violence. 



Deliberately paced and defined by a unique visual and sonic style, this haunting and emotional film is an unforgettable sensory experience. 



– Paul Ridd








Book now


















Fuga (Escape) is the continuation of our last film By the Name of Tania which was also shot in the Peruvian Amazon. Our experience with vulnerable populations forges deep ties leading us from one film to another. Fuga explores the stories of homosexuals persecuted by the Tupac Amaru and Shining Path terrorist groups during the “dirty war” in Peru (1970-2000). This generation, which survived persecution in silence and shame, has yet to be heard and recognised.



We worked with queer artist Saor Sax. Sometimes male, sometimes female, he is pure insolence for an Amazon society plagued by evangelistic morality. It is through his quest that Fuga makes the link between present and past. Saor discovers Valentina’s life through those who knew her as Pol, before her transformation, during the years of terrorism.



By telling their love story and revisiting Valentina’s troubled past, Fuga draws a portrait of this absent woman of double identity and lifts the curtain on a complex historic reality.



– Directors Mary Jiménez and Bénédicte Liénard
Warnings: Animal cruelty, Death and dying, Homophobia and heterosexism
